Block Merging

Block merging for structured grids via face matching.

This module provides functions to merge structured grid blocks (Plot3D format) by detecting and aligning matching faces between adjacent blocks. It supports arbitrary face-pair combinations (e.g., imax-jmin, jmax-imin) through transposition and flipping of block geometry arrays, and groups blocks into nxnxn cube clusters for batch merging using connectivity graph information.

plot3d.block_merging_mixed_facepairs.rotate_block_to_align_faces(X, Y, Z, face_from: str, face_to: str)[source]

Rotate block geometry arrays so that face_from aligns with face_to.

Currently only the jmax -> imin rotation is implemented.

Parameters:

  • X (numpy.ndarray) – X-coordinate array of shape (ni, nj, nk).

  • Y (numpy.ndarray) – Y-coordinate array of shape (ni, nj, nk).

  • Z (numpy.ndarray) – Z-coordinate array of shape (ni, nj, nk).

  • face_from (str) – Name of the source face on the block being rotated (e.g. 'jmax').

  • face_to (str) – Name of the target face on the receiving block (e.g. 'imin').

Returns:

The rotated (X, Y, Z) arrays with the same element count but reordered axes.

Return type:

tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray]

Raises:

NotImplementedError – If the requested (face_from, face_to) combination is not yet supported.

plot3d.block_merging_mixed_facepairs.combine_2_blocks_mixed_pairing(block1, block2, tol=1e-08)[source]

Merge two structured blocks by matching and aligning any pair of faces.

Detects the matching face pair between block1 and block2, then transposes and flips block2 so that its coordinate arrays align with block1 along the stacking axis. If the dominant physical step direction is inconsistent between the two blocks, block1 is also flipped before concatenation. Cross-axis face combinations (e.g. imax-jmin) are handled by transposing the index axes of block2.

Parameters:

  • block1 (Block) – The first structured block. May be flipped in-place along the stacking axis when physical directions are inconsistent.

  • block2 (Block) – The second structured block whose geometry is transposed and flipped to match block1.

  • tol (float, optional) – Coordinate tolerance used by find_matching_faces(). Defaults to 1e-8.

Returns:

A new Block containing the merged, standardised grid.

Return type:

Block

plot3d.block_merging_mixed_facepairs.combine_blocks_mixed_pairs(blocks: List[Block], tol: float = 1e-08, max_tries: int = 4) → Tuple[List[Block], List[int]][source]

Merge as many blocks as possible from a group via greedy face matching.

Iterates over all block pairs in blocks and merges any pair whose faces match within tol. Passes are repeated up to max_tries times to allow chains of merges to complete.

Parameters:

  • blocks (List[Block]) – Input blocks to merge, typically up to 8 blocks forming a cube cluster.

  • tol (float, optional) – Coordinate tolerance passed to find_matching_faces(). Defaults to 1e-8.

  • max_tries (int, optional) – Maximum number of greedy merge passes. Defaults to 4.

Returns:

A 2-tuple containing:

  • merged_blocks (List[Block]): Resulting blocks after all possible merges; may still contain more than one element if some blocks could not be joined.

  • used_indices (List[int]): Indices (into the original blocks list) of every block consumed during merging.

Return type:

tuple[List[Block], List[int]]

plot3d.block_merging_mixed_facepairs.combine_nxnxn_cubes_mixed_pairs(blocks: List[Block], connectivities: List[List[Dict]], cube_size: int = 2, tol: float = 1e-08) → List[Tuple[Block, Set[int]]][source]

Find and merge all non-overlapping nxnxn cube groups of blocks.

Builds a connectivity graph from connectivities, then repeatedly seeds BFS from unvisited block indices to gather candidate groups of exactly cube_size**3 connected blocks. Each valid group is forwarded to combine_blocks_mixed_pairs(). Blocks that cannot be grouped or merged are appended individually to the result.

Parameters:

  • blocks (List[Block]) – All input block objects indexed consistently with connectivities.

  • connectivities (List[List[Dict]]) – Face match metadata produced by the connectivity analysis, used to build the block adjacency graph.

  • cube_size (int, optional) – Side length of the block cube to attempt (e.g. 2 for 2x2x2 = 8 blocks, 4 for 4x4x4 = 64 blocks). Defaults to 2.

  • tol (float, optional) – Coordinate tolerance forwarded to combine_blocks_mixed_pairs(). Defaults to 1e-8.

Returns:

Each entry is a 2-tuple of:

  • merged_block (Block): The merged (or unmerged single) block.

  • source_indices (Set[int]): Indices into blocks of every original block that contributed to merged_block.

Return type:

List[Tuple[Block, Set[int]]]
